claim: Pilz Netherlands markets machinery risk assessment, safety concepts, system integration, validation and international conformity assessment as one lifecycle service.
The corrected consolidated Machinery Regulation replaces Directive 2006/42/EC and applies from 20 January 2027.

Article 10 requires the manufacturer to prepare technical documentation, carry out conformity assessment, draw up the EU declaration and affix CE marking before placing machinery on the market or putting it into service.
Article 18 treats a person carrying out a substantial modification as the manufacturer for the affected machinery or, in some assemblies, the affected part identified by the risk assessment.
Directive (EU) 2024/2853 treats a substantial modifier outside the original manufacturer's control as a manufacturer and applies to products put into service after 8 December 2026.
Dutch government guidance describes the rules as expected to take effect on 9 December 2026.
ISO published ISO 10218-2:2025 in February 2025 for industrial robot applications and cells, covering integration, commissioning, operation and maintenance.
The accessible EU harmonised-standards record reviewed did not establish ISO 10218-2:2025 as cited under Regulation (EU) 2023/1230.

The Dutch Labour Inspectorate says a manufacturer ensures machinery meets European requirements and affixes CE, while an employer keeps the machine safe, avoids unsafe modifications, maintains it and has it inspected.
IFR says it counts industrial robot installations by country and publishes comprehensive data in the purchasable World Robotics report/database.

TNO's 2026 report says the Netherlands is not explicit in IFR's public 2025 material, cites a 2023 density of 264 robots per 10,000 manufacturing workers, and says large-scale cobot deployment in Dutch SMEs remains limited.
Dutch government guidance says machinery instructions must be supplied in a language users understand and, under the Machinery Directive, in the language of the country where the machine is marketed.
The cited legal duties attach to the manufacturer and do not establish a licensed outside CE-signatory role for the proposed consultant.
